Hi Jordan — great speaking earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call so we have alignment for Amaya Health's security/compliance review:

- SOC 2: You asked whether Redwood has an up-to-date SOC 2 Type II report and whether it includes the inference service. Short answer: yes — we completed a Type II for our production environment in 2024 and the inference runtime is in-scope. I'll attach the SOC 2 cover summary and coordinate a secure link to the full report.
- GDPR / HIPAA: Our platform supports data residency and controls to help with GDPR. For HIPAA, we offer a Business Associate Agreement and can enable PHI controls on Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Data retention/deletion: Standard hosted retention is configurable — default logs & activity retention is 90 days; primary customer data retention can be set per contract. You asked specifically about deletion SLAs and backups (including backups and KV caches).

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll loop in Neha (security) to start the vendor questionnaire and confirm backup/retention SLAs (especially deletion from backups and cache eviction behavior).
2) Marissa will follow up on commercial terms and map the Dedicated vs Hosted options relative to Amaya's privacy requirements.
3) We'll share the SOC 2 summary and a short data retention doc by EOD tomorrow.

If that looks right, we'll kick off the OneTrust questionnaire and copy you on the link. Anything I missed?

Thanks —
Rishi

Hi Rishi — thanks for the recap and for the quick call. A couple of clarifications from our security and privacy team:

- SOC 2: We'll need confirmation the report covers the inference endpoints used in hosted mode (not just internal admin services). Is the full report available under an NDA or a secure portal?
- Deletion SLA: Can you confirm the SLA for deletion of customer data initiated by Amaya? We need a formal SLA window (e.g., 30/60/90 days) and details on deletion from backups — specifically whether backups are overwritten, encrypted, and how long they are retained.
- KV cache and ephemeral storage: Does Redwood persist KV caches to backups or are they ephemeral and evicted on session expiration? For HIPAA scoping, we need to know if PHI could persist in any backup or long-term logs.

We'll also start the vendor security questionnaire on our side — happy to take the OneTrust link when you send it.

Appreciate the quick follow-up.
-Jordan
Director of Platform Security | Amaya Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Rishi / Marissa — see answers below you can pass to Jordan + Priya. I've included short attachments (SOC2 summary, retention doc). If they need the full Type II report we typically provide it via a secure portal after an NDA; include me in that request and I'll provision access.

1) SOC 2 coverage: The 2024 Type II includes the inference public endpoints in hosted mode; scope notes in the summary indicate model serving, request routing, and runtime were tested. Full report: available under NDA via our secure portal. (attachment: SOC2_Report_Redwood_2024.pdf)

2) Deletion SLA (hosted):
- Customer-initiated deletion: We guarantee logical deletion from the primary store within 30 days of a validated request.
- Backups: Backups are encrypted at rest; snapshots are retained for 60 days by default. Deletion from backups is handled via normal retention window policies — we do not offer immediate scrub from immutable backup snapshots without a contract amendment. For customers with stricter needs, we recommend Dedicated/Private deployment where you control snapshot lifecycle or we can negotiate a reduced backup retention as part of the contract (typically 7/30/60 day options).

3) KV cache and ephemeral storage:
- KV caches are ephemeral and reside in memory on serving nodes; we do not persist KV cache entries to long-term backup snapshots. They are evicted according to cache TTL and node lifecycle. For Hosted customers, caches may persist in memory for the session duration and are cleared on node recycle.

4) Logs & audit trails:
- Operational logs: 90-day retention by default for hosted accounts (can be extended).
- Request logs: full request metadata (no model outputs by default) retained 30 days; payload retention policies are configurable.

5) HIPAA / PHI guidance:
- For PHI workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments and execution of a BAA. In hosted mode, we can scope controls and provide documentation but BAA + Dedicated gives you full control over backups and retention windows.

Next steps I recommend we offer to Jordan: share the SOC 2 summary now, provide NDA+portal link for the full report on request, and kick off the OneTrust questionnaire (I can pre-fill security answers).

-Neha
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
